## Task 1

**To complete this task, first I loaded the tidyverse library.**

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse) #load tidyverse library
```

**Then, I used the readr package to load the college.data.csv file into an object called college_data.** 

```{r}
college_data <- read_csv("./data/collegedata.csv") #load collegedata.csv
```

## Task 2

**Even though the read_csv command gives you a message with the number of rows and columns, you can also use the dplyr command "glimpse" to see these details:**

```{r}
glimpse(college_data) #view the rows and column information for the dataframe
```

**Using either method, we find out that there are 7175 rows and 12 columms in this dataframe.**
